flagged_sentences: In 2005 the Federal Highway Administration examined 132 camera-equipped intersections in seven U.S. jurisdictions and recorded a 24.6 percent drop in right-angle crashes alongside a 14.9 percent rise in rear-end collisions.
The Campbell Collaboration’s 2020 systematic review of 38 studies confirmed an average 19 percent rise in rear-end collisions once regression-to-the-mean adjustments were applied.

claims.claim: The 2007 Virginia Transportation Research Council report found rear-end crashes increased 27 percent or 42 percent depending on method, with net increases in crash costs across six Northern Virginia jurisdictions from 1998 to 2004.
claims.episode_span: The Virginia Transportation Research Council’s 2007 analysis of the same Northern Virginia corridors found rear-end crashes rose between 27 and 42 percent depending on the statistical method, with substantial variation across jurisdictions.
claims.source_title: The Impact of Red-Light Cameras (Photo-red Enforcement) on Crashes in Virginia
claims.supporting_quote: This study finds that cameras are associated with an increase in rear-end crashes (about 27% or 42% depending on the statistical method used as shown in Tables ES1 and H1).

claims.claim: The Campbell Collaboration 2020 systematic review found red-light cameras increase rear-end crashes by about 19 percent after controlling for regression to the mean.
